questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That they have a different law system than ours and thus it would be interesting to learn about the differences. Moreover, Australia has a very unique culture and is situated on the other side of the world which I wanted to learn more about.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved going on exchange but I found the application process to be very complicated. This was due to my host university changing the offered subjects after my arrival.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. They have an information desk specifically to exchange students. However, the respond time was a bit slowly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed assistance with choosing my subjects as they kept on changing the course catalogue.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. Sydney is experiencing a rental crisis so my friends and I had to reach out to multiple people in the beginning. An advice is to be a part of the different Facebook-groups that exist for Danes in Sydney as some post about their rentals there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very nice if you want to get a more "local" vibe and be more connected to a neighborhood. At the same time, it also makes a bit difficult to connect with other exchange students. I struggled a lot with that at least.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to upload some formal documents and then fill out a form. It was a bit old-fashioned but quite easy to understand.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an e-mail you could send questions to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. The ones that I had wished for was not offered the session due to catalogue changes. However, I found others that were also quite interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time as there is a lot of waiting in the application process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took classes that was only available to MA-students. Some of the classes were easy to follow but other's demanded some pre-knowledge which made them a bit difficult in the beginning.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Class participation was a part of the grade in almost all classes. Moreover, we had to do multiple assessment tasks throughout the sessions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1. Justice, 2. Principles of Public International Law, 3. Trade Marks Law and 4. Dispute Resolution.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All classes - except Trade Marks Law. The others were easy to understand and with very sweet and motivating teachers. Trade Marks Law required some pre-knowledge and all the other students were professionals so the academic level was much higher.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food (especially groceries) was much more expensive than in Denmark. Sometimes takeaway was cheaper but that meant that I spent a lot more on food than I normally budget.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was multiple clubs, including sports and socials. Also there was a social hangout spot and different activities as food tastings and parties throughout the session.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend showing up on Orientation Day to hear from all the clubs and get a feeling of what you find exciting. Personally, I found the hangout spot to be quite fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Either do a roadtrip up the East or West Coast in a van. It is a bit expensive but so worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy due to it being a Western culture as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Come to the introductory arrangements as they will also be attending.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not really anything that was difficult. However, I quickly learned that Australians are much in debate about the Aborigines and their legal standing and, therefore, it was important to learn about the issues as it came up in most discussions.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were super laid back, welcoming and positive.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. To show up for orientation events to get to know a lot of other students. 2. There are surprisingly many exchange students (especially from Denmark). 3. It is very modern and situated in the city which is super nice for sightseeing in breaks.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to engage a lot in your subjects as you will have to submit a lot of assignments throughout the session as well as participate in class.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the different spots I got to visit and the new friends I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing and having to participate in all classes. It can be a bit intimidating when you sometimes do not know a lot about the subject or the issues discussed. However, I found the teachers and classmates to be very supportive.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No, I think that covers it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
